to increase team morale a happy team is a successful one. it is important that leaders congratulate their team when things are going well and give the team encouragement when they are not going so well. to direct a group leaders in the air cadets help steer the direction they want their team members to go by showing them how to complete a task and delegating task roles when needed. to perform tasks a good team gets things done and a good leader gives team members tasks, checking that they are being completed successfully. they make decisions and think ahead. administration good administration means that messages and information are passed on effectively to those who need it. this helps teams to perform tasks more effectively. leadership qualities why do we need good leaders? turn the dial to find out why the the royal air force air cadets need good leaders. 1 4 3 2 i

the smeac brief why do we need to use smeac? if you are in charge of a task your team need to know what is happening. the best way to do this is to give them a briefing. a clear briefing will include all of the important information needed to complete the task. a good leader will also check that their team members have understood by asking and answering questions. in the military the acronym smeac is often used as a tool to help deliver effective briefings.

you must click and on view each part of the smeac sequence before you can continue. the smeac brief what does smeac mean? s s s s m m m m e e e e a a a a c c c c each letter in smeac outlines a different part of the briefing sequence. find out what is needed for each section of a smeac brief by clicking on a letter.

click to close smeac - situation the bigger picture s m e a c smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu click to view the video an example of how to deliver the situation section of a smeac brief. example brief example brief example brief example brief example brief example brief this section provides your team with an overview of what’s going on. it details where you are, why you are there and what has happened/ about to happen. it is the bigger picture and gives context for the rest of the brief. it must be kept short and relevant.

smeac - any questions clarifying points s m e a c smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu click to view the video an example of how to deliver the any questions section of a smeac brief. this is where you ask your team if they have any questions. answer a question by reading the relevant part of the brief again. be confident when you do this! asking each team member individually if they have a question will help ensure that all team members get a chance to ask a question if they need to.

click to close smeac - execution how to complete the task s m e a c smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu click to view the video an example of how to deliver the execution section of a smeac brief. example brief example brief example brief example brief example brief example brief this is the most important part; telling your team the plan. ask your team for ideas if you don’t have any yourself and ensure that your team understands what they have to do to deliver the plan. in this section you should also tell your team about any limitations (rules) that must be followed when completing the task. all team members must understand what these limitations are.

click to close smeac - mission an outline of the task s m e a c smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu click to view the video an example of how to deliver the mission section of a smeac brief. example brief example brief example brief example brief example brief example brief this section provides an overview of what you need to do to complete your task. it must be short and snappy. the mission is to… in order to… this part of the brief is repeated twice to ensure your team have taken it in.

smeac - check understanding check the team are ready to go s m e a c smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu smeac menu ask your team questions to check that they have understood the briefing. ask each team member a different question and make sure they can answer it. if they can’t, re-read that section of the brief and consider asking the question again. finish with a positive message. click to view the video an example of how to deliver the check understanding section of a smeac brief.

leading your team the blue badge leadership assessment to gain your blue badge you will be assessed leading a small team. you will be assessed on how you perform as a leader in ten different areas. in each area you can score between one and five points. if you score one point on anything you will need to try again and be re-assessed. you must score at least 30 out of 50. the next page gives more information about each of the ten assessed areas.

click to close 10. did you give praise and encouragement throughout? click to close do's (tips for a higher score) give your team praise regularly when things are going well. encourage them when things are not going so well. keep your praise and encouragement brief but frequent. don’ts (things to avoid) don’t forget to do this. it’s easy to forget to praise your team when you are concentrating on the task. this is an area that new leaders frequently forget to monitor. avoid being negative. this brings everyone in the team down. 9. if an assessor had just entered the room, would they be able to tell who was in charge? click to close do's (tips for a higher score) ensure you stay separate from your team members when you brief them. regularly check that your team know what they are doing and ask if they are doing ok. consider taking a step back during the task so you get an overview of what is going on. don’ts (things to avoid) don’t allow other team members to take over or do the talking for you. don’t give up if things go wrong. be confident, take a step back and re-evaluate. 8. were you confident? click to close do's (tips for a higher score) stand up tall and make sure all of your team can hear you. state your smeac brief and plan with confidence. keep confident throughout the task. don’ts (things to avoid) don’t slouch, look grumpy or disinterested. don’t be overly loud or quiet. don’t let other team members try to take over. if they do, politely remind them to stop. 7. were the limitations monitored? click to close do's (tips for a higher score) make sure your team are following the task limitations throughout the task. ensure that your team member in charge of standards is positioned correctly so they can see what is going on. don’ts (things to avoid) don’t forget about monitoring the limitations. this is easy to do when you are concentrating on the task. don’t ignore the limitations on purpose when you think no-one is looking. this is dishonest and could mean you fail the task. 6. did the rest of the team know what was meant to be happening? click to close do's (tips for a higher score) regularly check up on your team members. are they happy? do they know what they are doing? take a step back and watch. are the team performing as they should? don’ts (things to avoid) don’t assume your team members know what they are doing just because you told them. check they actually understand their task. don’t be afraid to stop the task and re-brief the team if it’s not going well. 5. did you re-evaluate when something went wrong? click to close do's (tips for a higher score) keep calm when something goes wrong. be flexible and adapt – if you are doing the same thing over and over and it doesn’t work you are just wasting time. don’ts (things to avoid) don’t be afraid to stop, take a step back and re-evaluate the plan. don’t keep a new idea to yourself. tell your team about any changes to the plan. 4. was there an initial plan? click to close do's (tips for a higher score) think of a rough plan before you brief your team. use the back of your smeac briefing notes sheet to jot down ideas quickly if needed. try to think about what could go wrong during the task and try and formulate your plan to take this into account. don’ts (things to avoid) don’t be afraid to ask your team for ideas if you are not sure, but don’t be over reliant on your team members to think of an idea for you. you are in charge and the overall plan must be yours. don’t let other team members take over. 3. did you mention and monitor the time limitation? do's (tips for a higher score) one of your team should be in charge of timings to ensure that you are following any time limitations. regularly ask for time updates to make sure you are on track. don’ts (things to avoid) don’t forget to check you have enough time left. this is an area that new leaders frequently forget to monitor. don’t rush. this can lead to mistakes and actually slow you down. click to close 2. did you mention all the limitations? click to close do's (tips for a higher score) write down and understand the limitations (rules of the task) before you start. one of your team should be in charge of standards to ensure that everyone is following the task limitations. use smeac to check your teams understanding. don’ts (things to avoid) don’t forget to mention all the limitations. if your team don’t have this information then they cannot succeed. don’t assume that your team understand what the limitations are. encourage them to ask questions during the smeac brief and throughout the task to check their understanding. 1. did you brief using smeac? do's (tips for a higher score) use the smeac briefing notes sheet. this can be found in the resources section. listen to your instructor carefully when they are passing on the brief to you; write down as much as you can and ask questions to clarify key points. brief your team in the correct order. don’ts (things to avoid) don’t forget to assign the 2ic, timekeeper and standards roles. this will help you later. don’t brief out of order; this will confuse your team and you will miss key points. don’t try to remember everything without writing it down. in the heat of the moment you will probably forget something. click to close you are assessed across ten areas. click on the boxes below to find out some do’s and don’ts. leading your team tips for success did you brief using smeac? did you mention all the limitations? did you mention and monitor the time limitation? was there an initial plan? did you re-evaluate when something went wrong? did the rest of the team know what was meant to be happening? were limitations monitored? were you confident? if an assessor had just entered the room, would they be able to tell who was in charge? did you give praise and encouragement throughout? example assessment sheet click here to view the assessment sheet your instructor will use during your leadership task.
